title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in 'variations sur l'équation des lacets', Grothendieck replaces the profinite free group on x, y (the Grothendieck–Teichmüller setting) by a linear group scheme G over a base S. G is a form of GL(2), with SG ≃ SL(2)_S and central G_m. He fixes two sections ρ and σ of G. In the model case on the next page, ρ = [[0,1],[-1,1]] and σ = [[0,-1],[1,0]], of orders 6 and 4 in GL2, hence 3 and 2 projectively. He has built a group scheme G*_{ρ,σ} with sections (α, β, μ, ε), where ε = ±1 marks the component of the normalizer N'_σ. He also has a morphism Θ : G*_{ρ,σ} → B'_0 × T_ρ × N'_σ, with u = Θ(α, β, μ, ε) a section of G. Here T_ρ and T_σ are the centralizers of ρ and σ, and N'_σ is a normalizer-type group of σ.

Formulas (29) describe u through conjugation:
- u ρ u^{-1} = ξ ρ, with ξ = α ρ(α)^{-1}. Here ρ(·) means conjugation by ρ, and the factor written ρ(λ) is the same as int(λ)ρ, i.e. a twisted conjugate.
- u σ u^{-1} = η σ, with η = ε β σ β^{-1} σ^{-1}, i.e. u σ u^{-1} = ε · int(β)(σ). He warns 'attention au facteur ε!'.
- det u = μ.
This is the linear-algebraic analogue of the GT-type action x ↦ x^λ, y ↦ f^{-1} y^λ f, now realised by inner automorphisms of G twisted by the sign ε.

Proposition: Θ is characterized by (29) up to multiplication by a morphism of schemes G_{ρ,σ} → μ_2. Proof:
- The action on ρ determines u modulo the centralizer T_ρ.
- The action on σ determines u modulo T_σ.
- Together they determine u modulo T_ρ ∩ T_σ = G_m. This holds because ρ and σ generate the full matrix algebra, so their common centralizer is the centre.
- The determinant then fixes u modulo G_m ∩ SG = μ_2, since det restricted to G_m is t ↦ t^2.
- Hence any other Θ' satisfying (29) has the form Θ'(g) = λ(g) Θ(g), with λ : G_{ρ,σ} → μ_2.

Remark: the normalization Θ(1,1,1,1) = 1 forces λ(1) = 1. When ρ and σ are regular, T_ρ and T_σ are tori. If moreover the char is ≠ 2 (μ_2 étale) and the relevant group (B'_0 × T_ρ × T_σ) has connected fibres, λ is then trivial. What remains is the sign indeterminacy on the ε = -1 component, coming from N'_σ/T_σ ≃ Z/2 and its action on μ_2. This is presumably why the next section (IX) introduces the groups SM_{ρ,σ} = SG*_{ρ,σ} ×_S SG and the homomorphism Ĝ_{0,3} → GL(2, Ẑ)^{±1}/(±1).
errors: The letter λ is used twice on the page: in int(λ) / ρ(λ) as a group element (apparently the same as α), and as the μ_2-valued correcting morphism. This makes the text ambiguous.

The triviality argument for λ needs G_{ρ,σ} (or the relevant component) to have connected fibres, and μ_2 to be étale (char ≠ 2). Grothendieck flags both only parenthetically. On the ε = -1 component of N'_σ the normalization λ(1) = 1 does not force λ = 1, so a genuine sign indeterminacy remains there. The marginal note seems to acknowledge this.
The step T_ρ ∩ T_σ = G_m tacitly assumes that ρ and σ generate the full matrix algebra in every fibre (an irreducibility condition). This is presumably part of the 'conditions générales' on ρ and σ.

ideas.what: Describing a lift u in a GL2-form by its conjugation action on two fixed elements ρ, σ plus its determinant; uniqueness up to μ_2 via the intersection of centralizers being the centre.
ideas.modern_name: Rigidity of elements of GL2 modulo centre via centralizers; linear (GL2-valued) model of Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type actions on a pair of generators of orders 3 and 2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard linear algebra / group-scheme theory. The GT framework is due to Drinfeld (1990) and Ihara.
ideas.where_published: Only in these unpublished notes (sequel to La Longue Marche)

ideas.what: Indeterminacy of the normalized solution Θ by a μ_2-valued function, killed by connectedness except on the non-identity component of the normalizer of σ.
ideas.modern_name: Sign ambiguity in lifting from PGL2 to GL2 / component group of the normalizer of a torus

missed.claim: Part of Grothendieck's unpublished programme of 'linearizing' the loop equation: modelling the action of GT-type data (λ, f) by group schemes G*_{ρ,σ} attached to a pair (ρ, σ) in a GL2-form. This leads on the next page to a homomorphism Ĝ_{0,3} → GL(2, Ẑ)^{±1}/(±1). The page itself contains only a routine uniqueness lemma.
missed.quote: Le morphisme de schémas Θ est caractérisé par les formules (29), mod un morphisme G_{ρ,σ} → μ_2
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of interest mainly as documentation of how Grothendieck intended to map the GT group to linear groups over Ẑ (cf. later work on GT and SL2(Ẑ)/modular representations). The lemma itself is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine uniqueness-up-to-μ_2 lemma within a larger unpublished construction. The interest lies in the surrounding programme, not this page.
transcription_corrections: 'λ : G_{ρ,σ} → E_2' should read 'λ : G_{ρ,σ} → μ_2'.
'BS'_0 × T_ρ × T_σ' should be 'B'_0 × T_ρ × T_σ' (B'_0 as on the previous page).
In the first line of (29), the definition of ξ is 'ξ = α ρ(α)^{-1}' (or 'αρ(λ)^{-1}'). The second line reads 'u(σ) = ε int(β)(σ)' (u ρ u^{-1} = int(λ)ρ), and 'déf' sits under u(ρ).
'(dans ... car. ≠ 2)' likely reads '(dans le cas car. ≠ 2)'.
The symbol above the top of the page appears to be 'Θ(φ)' / '4φ0', not part of the formula.
